newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka's Wayamba buys strategic stake in Malwatte.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka's Wayamba buys strategic stake in Malwatte.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Wayamba Plantations (Pte) Ltd said it bought a strategic 51 percent stake in Malwatte Valley Plantations Ltd, which was sold on the stock exchange by the government on Friday.
Wayamba said in a statement that it bought the company's 10-rupee share for 61 rupees after they were put on bid on the stock exchange at a minimum price of 40 rupees.

An official of the government's privatisation arm, Public Enterprise Reform Commission (PERC), said on Thursday that Wayamba was one of the three groups which qualified to bid for a 51 percent strategic stake in four plantations, which the government was selling on the Colombo Stock Exchange.
The PERC said three more plantations will be sold on the stock exchange this month. A strategic stake in Kahawatte will be sold on July 7, Elpitiya on July 8 and Elkaduwa a day later.
The shares of these three will be introduced at a minimum price of 30 rupees for each 10-rupee share.
The two other bidders are a consortium led by Aitken Spence & Co and another led by Forbes Ceylon Ltd.
Sri Lanka began restructuring its ailing plantation sector by privatising management of 23 plantations, which own some 600,000 hectares of tea, rubber and coconut land, in 1992.
Privatistion began in 1995 when it sold 51 percent or 10.2 million shares to a strategic investor, gave 10 percent to workers and the balance to the public.
The government retains one "golden share", which allows it to intervene in case of mismanagement.
